textbookText: 56. Division of complex numbers z₁/z₂ is typically performed by: A) Multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator to rationalize it B) Dividing the real parts and imaginary parts separately without any conjugate C) Subtracting the arguments directly without considering the modulus D) It is never possible to divide complex numbers
57. A complex number z is called purely real when: A) Its imaginary part equals zero (z = a + 0i) B) Its real part equals zero C) Its modulus equals zero D) Its argument equals 90°

58. The relationship between exponential form and trigonometric form of a complex number, known as Euler's formula, is: A) e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ B) e^(iθ) = cos θ − i sin θ C) e^(iθ) = i(cos θ + sin θ) D) e^(iθ) = θ
59. Which of these correctly relates argument of conjugate z̄ to argument of z? A) arg(z̄) = −arg(z) B) arg(z̄) = arg(z) C) arg(z̄) = 180° − arg(z) always D) arg(z̄) is undefined

60. An extraordinary application: complex numbers are used to represent impedance in AC circuits because: A) They naturally encode both magnitude and phase relationships between voltage and current using real and imaginary components B) They eliminate the need for any calculation involving resistance C) They only apply to direct current (DC) circuits D) They convert AC circuits into purely mechanical systems
